note: Mappings XDJ-700 v1.15 -> XDJ-1000 MK1 v1.13 found by tracing/behaviour in cdj-nxs2 qemu (2026-11-01). 'unverified': false only where a behaviour test passed in the emulator. Never tested on hardware. Re-verified on QEMU 11.1.2 after the cdj-nxs2 update (same results).

touch_parser.evidence: both 59 literals; 12 slots agree with the step-2 map, 0 conflict; slot #53 holds the hit-tester on both; parser+0xBE4 is the same 'mov.l @slot,r10' with identical following code
touch_parser.behaviour: the function its slot #53 points to receives every touch (see hit_tester)

hit_tester.evidence: value of parser slot #53 on both; same call shape ext,ext,ext,A,B,A,C,B,A,C,D; 16/16 literals
hit_tester.behaviour: CDJ_FWTRACE at entry: r4=1 while pressed, r5 = tapped x (MK1 154/576/394, 700 394/240), 0 otherwise

hit_tester_A.evidence: callee position A in the identical call shape; runs only while touching (MK1 trace)

touch_only_small.evidence: 20 insns, one 0xA80Dxxxx literal, directly before the zone-accessor run on both

bj_dispatcher.evidence: owns six stubs 'mov #n,r4; add #8,r15; bra handler; lds.l @r15+,pr' (n=6..1) on both
bj_dispatcher.behaviour: CDJ_PCALL2 anchored here calls the handler in its own task context on both

bj_handler.evidence: only match of the 10-insn head pattern in each image; tail-jumped by the 6 dispatcher stubs; MK1 trace: runs only in the six beat-jump windows
bj_handler.behaviour: r4 = 1..6 = <<1 >>1 <<2 >>2 <<4 >>4. Stock MK1 pads call it once per tap with those codes (FWTRACE). Direct calls (CDJ_PCALL2) move REMAIN by +0.54 -0.39 +0.91 -0.96 +1.93 -2.00 s on MK1 and +0.55 -0.48 +1.07 -0.85 +2.13 -1.93 s on the 700 (1 beat = 0.499 s, noise about 0.1 s)

touch_hook_slot_load.evidence: touch_parser+0xBE4 on both: 'mov.l @(disp,pc),r10' loading the hook slot, identical next words 09dc e0f8 600c 649c
touch_hook_slot_load.behaviour: poking the slot from this instruction disconnects every touch (see touch_hook_slot)

touch_hook_slot.evidence: touch_parser literal slot #53; stock value 0x08dd0128 / 0x08d76ce8 (the hit-testers)
touch_hook_slot.behaviour: redirect test (QEMU 11.1.2, 2026-11-01): CDJ_PPOKE at the slot load (0x08cf93ae) set the slot to a stock 'rts; mov #0,r0' stub (0x08ae2248): hit-tester passes 0 (control 2593), a tap on <<4 called no handler and did not jump (REMAIN 1:02.480 vs baseline 1:02.384; control +2.03 s). The slot is the live touch hook.

bj_size_row_rev1.evidence: unique 44-byte match: 8-byte entries (beats, direction) for codes 1..6 = (1,1)(1,0)(2,1)(2,0)(4,1)(4,0); same following data
bj_size_row_rev1.behaviour: PPOKE at handler entry: code-1 entry 1->8 then call code 1: +3.94 s (8 beats = 3.99 s)

bj_size_row_fwd1.evidence: entry for code 2 in the same table
bj_size_row_fwd1.behaviour: PPOKE code-2 entry 1->16 then call code 2: -8.09 s (16 beats = 7.99 s)

touch_zone_state.evidence: hit_tester literal slot #0 (16/16) + the 10 zone accessors after it (25 insns each, both literals) on both: 21 votes, 0 against
touch_zone_state.behaviour: sampled every 20 ms: 700 idle 0x1E, hot-cue row 0x19, beat-loop pad 0x16; MK1 idle 0x23, hot-cue row 0x1E, beat-jump pad 0x16
touch_zone_state.PORTING_NOTE: values differ: the mod's 'new press' test (== 0x1E, i.e. no zone on the 700) must use 0x23 on MK1; 0x1E on MK1 is the hot-cue row

key_bitmap_93.evidence: parser literals #2/#3: 0x0b6c7a28/0x0b6c7a5c (700) vs 0x0e0c79e0/0x0e0c7a14 (MK1), same 0x34 spacing; same offset assumed for the key bitmap
key_bitmap_93.behaviour: not tested: setting the bit by gdbstub or at the dispatcher did not trigger a jump on the 700 either (the mod re-asserts it inside the touch path)
